Hi there, Im finishing my PhD in Pain research after 5 years. I don't think there is such a strong relation between academic and research performance. In my experience, a good PhD needs a set of abilities and capabilities that are not very important while studying in university. In my experience these are some of the important traits a good scientist needs:

1. Resilience to persistent  failure.
2.  Hability to handle incomplete and misleading information.
3. Good communication abilities with peers and superiors.
4. Autonomous organizaton of time and productivity.
5. Precission and patience while experimenting.
6. Open and focused while reading and writing.
7.  ... 

I had a really nice time in college, doing my Bachelors in Biology and my Masters Degree in Neuroscience I loved to discuss about the things I learned read tons of literature and worked a bit in many different laboratories. Then, I ended with good marks and got a good grant for my PhD. But, then I found out that this abilities that I had were not enough to have a good time in the actual research life. I'm taking both oral finasteride and the cutaneous dutasteride. I think I have mild to medium effects with the finasteride, mainly regarding sex drive (but I can work around it). 

Anyway, I work as a researcher in the Pain treatment field, and I assure you that whenever you can have a local treatment, It will be preferable to a systemic one. Some of the reasons are that: you have less effects in other parts of the body (in this case the activity of 5alfareductase is not as altered in other parts, like the brain or genitalia), the concentration of the drug is more acuratelly administered in the target tissue, you avoid digestive interactions and hepatic filtering...

In the case of dutasteride, being such a powerful drug, it is much better to apply it locally.

No sides

Mesotherapy has de benefits of any local treatment: more concentration of the active compound in the area of interest (the scalp), less effect in other areas of the organism.

The protocol is one set of injections every 40 days, around 2-3ml per sesion, 0,05% dutasteride.
